title: UI compatibility sweep: Safari & Firefox + mobile layout triage for tokens, buttons, tables, charts
creator: Asha Patel
description: Comprehensive QA sweep of the design system components across Safari (macOS & iOS) and Firefox (desktop) plus responsive checks on common mobile viewports. Focus areas: design tokens (spacing, type, color), primary/secondary button variants, responsive table layouts, and chart axis/grid alignment. Goal is to triage and produce prioritized bug list with engineering-actionable fixes and design decisions for platform inconsistencies.
affected_components: Table: responsive collapse and horizontal scroll
Chart: grid alignment, axis label clipping
Forms: input placeholder color and autofill background
steps_to_reproduce: Load component sandbox (components.redwood.design) in latest macOS Safari (v16.x) and iOS Safari on iPhone 14 simulator
Open same sandbox in Firefox Desktop (v113) and Chrome for baseline comparison
Resize viewport to 375x812 (iPhone portrait) and 360x800 (Android) and observe responsive behavior
Toggle reduced-motion and high-contrast in OS preferences to check focus and visual affordances
Compare computed CSS token values (devtools) between browsers to identify token parsing differences
observed_behavior: Safari (macOS): subtle baseline shift in body font on first paint causing button vertical alignment to appear off by 1-2px
iOS Safari: backdrop-filter on modal header causes heavy rendering and blurs incorrectly when chart canvas is present
Firefox: subpixel rounding causes chart gridlines and axis tick labels to misalign at smaller widths
Tables: horizontal overflow behavior differs — Safari collapses rows earlier, Firefox shows unexpected horizontal scrollbar breaking sticky header alignment
Buttons: .btn--ghost uses -webkit-appearance in Safari leading to unwanted inner shadow on iOS; touch target on mobile variant sometimes <44px in height when padding tokens applied inconsistently
expected_behavior: Tokens should render consistently across browsers so components keep visual parity within 1px tolerance
Buttons should maintain minimum touch target of 44x44 on mobile and consistent focus ring across UA/systems
Tables should gracefully allow horizontal scroll while keeping header sticky and column alignment preserved
Charts should render gridlines aligned with axis ticks across browsers at all responsive breakpoints
proposed_fixes: Normalize token output: add browser-specific overrides for font-synthesis and -webkit-font-smoothing in base.css and document reasoning in token spec
Replace backdrop-filter usage for critical modal headers with solid-color fallback + precomputed blur image for iOS Safari to avoid rendering jank
Introduce 1px snapping utility for canvas-based charts to counter subpixel rounding in Firefox (round to device pixel ratio) and add unit tests in chart rendering harness
Update table component to use container overflow:auto with min-width fallback and explicit sticky-header z-index to avoid stacking differences
Button variant: remove reliance on -webkit-appearance for ghost/secondary; enforce explicit box-shadow and border styles; update mobile padding tokens to ensure >=44px tap area
triage_decision: Categorized into P0 (touch target & modal rendering causing input blocking on iOS), P1 (visual misalignments that degrade perceived polish), and P2 (minor spacing subpixel differences). P0 items assigned to ENG-2048 and ENG-2052 for immediate fixes; P1 items scheduled for runtime-1.20; P2 tracked for next tokens sweep.
